findings.highlight: An electric heater. I'm not allowed to use a gas heater according to the front desk.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ああこれ？　電熱器。フロントに聞いたらガス使えないって」
findings.explanation: Setsuna is holding an electric hotplate because the hotel will not allow gas; she has brought it with pots, pans, and ingredients to cook for Kazusa. The English turns both appliances into room heaters, making the physical comedy and the next inventory incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「ああこれ？　電熱器。
フロントに聞いたらガス使えないって」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, this? An electric heater. I'm not allowed to use a gas heater according to the front desk."

findings.highlight: You're the one he's truly loved since five years ago, Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつは五年前から雪菜のことが好きだったよ。ずっとあいつを見てたあたしだからわかるんだよ…」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki liked Setsuna five years ago; she can tell because she was watching him. 'Truly loved' adds exclusivity and contradicts the surrounding argument that Kazusa remained his first and foremost love while Setsuna's effort eventually brought her level with or beyond Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
「あいつは五年前から雪菜のことが好きだったよ。
ずっとあいつを見てたあたしだからわかるんだよ…」
findings.todokanai: "You're the one he's truly loved since five years ago, Setsuna. I know that full well because I've been watching him all that time…"

findings.highlight: Even so, I'll never be able to become the one he loves most.
findings.evidenceJa: 「それでも、彼の中の一番はずっと変わらなかった。…途中からだけど、ずっと彼を見てるわたしならわかる」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki's number one had remained unchanged throughout that period. The English turns this retrospective observation into a permanent prediction that she will never become number one, immediately clashing with her next statement that her best was to draw level and Kazusa's answer that Setsuna ultimately did become the woman he loves most.
findings.japanese:
「それでも、彼の中の一番はずっと変わらなかった。
…途中からだけど、ずっと彼を見てるわたしならわかる」
findings.todokanai: "Even so, I'll never be able to become the one he loves most. …I know because I've always watched him, even if not for as long as you."

findings.highlight: You worked really hard while I couldn't.
findings.evidenceJa: 「でも雪菜は努力した。…あたしのしなかった努力をさ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Setsuna made the effort that she herself did not make. The English changes self-reproach for not acting into inability, mitigating the agency and responsibility on which Kazusa bases her concession of defeat.
findings.japanese:
「でも雪菜は努力した。
…あたしのしなかった努力をさ」
findings.todokanai: "But you worked really hard, Setsuna. …You worked really hard while I couldn't."

findings.highlight: There's no need for me to go out of my way to admit that, is there?
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前の勝ちだよ。もう勝負はついてる。…わざわざ、あたしに負けを認めさせなくてもいいだろ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa tells Setsuna there is no need for Setsuna to go out of her way to make Kazusa admit defeat. The English says Kazusa herself need not go out of her way to admit it, reversing the agency in her accusation that Setsuna is pressing the victory upon her.
findings.japanese:
「お前の勝ちだよ。もう勝負はついてる。
…わざわざ、あたしに負けを認めさせなくてもいいだろ」
findings.todokanai: "You win. The game is over. …There's no need for me to go out of my way to admit that, is there?"

findings.highlight: I like you, and you're already so close to me!
findings.evidenceJa: 「でも、でも…わたし、かずさに対して無関心じゃいられない。…好きと、ものすごく近いところにいるんだよ！」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she cannot be indifferent to Kazusa and that what she feels lies extremely close to love. The English instead says Kazusa is physically or emotionally close to Setsuna, changing the subject of 'close' and flattening Setsuna's difficult attempt to name her own feeling.
findings.japanese:
「でも、でも…
わたし、かずさに対して無関心じゃいられない。
…好きと、ものすごく近いところにいるんだよ！」
findings.todokanai: "Still, still… I just can't bring myself to not worry about you, Kazusa. …I like you, and you're already so close to me!"

findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつの言ってることは全部間違いだ。だってあいつは、人としてのセンスがないから」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki has no sense or talent for being a human being. She deliberately casts moral judgment as innate artistic センス, then extends the conceit through talent, artists, and Japanese people. 'Lacks common sense' turns this into conventional social judgment and breaks the sustained analogy.
findings.japanese:
「あいつの言ってることは全部間違いだ。
だってあいつは、人としてのセンスがないから」
findings.todokanai: "Everything that comes out of his mouth is wrong. After all, that guy lacks common sense."

findings.highlight: "Still, I don't think his mistakes can be attributed to his lack of sense. It's just that nothing was really ever fair from the very beginning."
findings.evidenceJa:
「でも、彼が間違いを犯すのは、
彼にセンスがないからじゃない。
ただ、最初から公平じゃないんだよ」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki is not impartial from the outset when reaching conclusions; 'nothing was ever fair' externalizes the bias into circumstances — Her explanation that he always favors Kazusa follows directly.
findings.japanese:
「でも、彼が間違いを犯すのは、
彼にセンスがないからじゃない。
ただ、最初から公平じゃないんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Still, I don't think his mistakes can be attributed to his lack of sense. It's just that nothing was really ever fair from the very beginning."

findings.highlight: the world of those five years past
findings.evidenceJa: 「けれど日本に来て、五年後の世界に来て…幸せな空想が、現実に壊された」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says that by coming to Japan she entered the world five years later—the present from which Vienna had insulated her—and reality destroyed her happy fantasy. The English calls it the world of five years past, reversing the temporal movement central to the scene.
findings.japanese:
「けれど日本に来て、五年後の世界に来て…
幸せな空想が、現実に壊された」
findings.todokanai: "But the moment I came to Japan, the world of those five years past… my fantasies of happiness had been destroyed by reality."

findings.highlight: The one person that I've always gone for has disappeared… the one person who's always supported me all this time is no more.
findings.evidenceJa: 「目指してた人が、あたしの先にいなくなった…ずっと支えてくれていた人が、消えてしまった」
findings.explanation: Kazusa distinguishes two losses: Youko, the person she aimed toward, is no longer ahead of her as a guiding goal; Haruki, the person who supported her, has disappeared from her life. The English describes both as simple disappearance and obscures why Setsuna immediately answers first about Youko and then about Haruki.
findings.japanese:
「目指してた人が、あたしの先にいなくなった…
ずっと支えてくれていた人が、消えてしまった」
findings.todokanai: "The one person that I've always gone for has disappeared… the one person who's always supported me all this time is no more."

findings.highlight: Even though I've known full well that they could never be a reality…
findings.evidenceJa: 「でも現実には、あたしの望みは何一つ叶わない。わかってたことだけど、永遠に知りたくなかった…っ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she knew none of her wishes would come true but wanted never, for all eternity, to know or confront that fact. The English omits the refusal to know and replaces it with the flatter claim that she knew the wishes could not become reality, losing the distinction between abstract knowledge and forced recognition.
findings.japanese:
「でも現実には、
あたしの望みは何一つ叶わない。
わかってたことだけど、永遠に知りたくなかった…っ」
findings.todokanai: "But the reality is that not even one of my wishes has come true. Even though I've known full well that they could never be a reality…"

findings.highlight: Stay by my side tonight, too.
findings.evidenceJa: 「もう、寝るよ。ありがと、雪菜。今夜も、側にいてくれて」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she is going to sleep and thanks Setsuna for having stayed beside her again tonight. The English changes completed companionship and gratitude into a fresh imperative that Setsuna remain, altering both tense and Kazusa's emotional gesture.
findings.japanese:
「もう、寝るよ。
ありがと、雪菜。
今夜も、側にいてくれて」
findings.todokanai: "Let's just go to sleep. Thank you, Setsuna. Stay by my side tonight, too."
